title: A new field in a shared synced entry must not make old merge rules see the entry as theirs
rule: When you add a field to an entry that several fields share in a synced file (a sidecar's familyMeta, a face entry), check every existing ancestor/merge function that reads that entry: an entry that is now written only for the new field must count as 'no entry' for the old fields, exactly as when the entry was absent before. Filter on the old field's presence (`disk.filter(|d| d.notes.is_some())`), or the old field's removal stops spreading. Add a two-machine test that clears the old field on one machine while the new field keeps the entry alive, and asserts the clear reaches the other machine.
rationale: E15.2 (#119): adding `license` to `FamilyEntry` kept a notes-less entry on disk; `family_ancestor` read it as a notes entry with no history, so notes cleared on one machine were written back by the teammate's machine.
